messages:
Maya: Heads-up: after canary deploy frontend-v6 we're seeing chart stutter on heatmaps and sparklines. p95 render latency jumped on some routes.
Ryan: Confirmed on prod-canary and my local canary profile. p95 ~120ms -> ~420ms for chart render. telemetry: https://telemetry.redwood/console/canary/heatmap
Devon: Which bundle diff landed in this deploy? Any big libs or polyfills added?
Maya: Build summary shows telemetry-client bumped to v1.5.0 and an intl polyfill got pulled into main. main.js gzip grew from ~2.4MB -> ~4.1MB. LongTask samples show parse+compile spikes.
Aj: That was my telemetry bump. v1.5.0 includes the opentelemetry shim and we accidentally included an intl-pluralrules polyfill for a small subset of locales.
Kevin: Also recall we raised KV prefetch concurrency for heatmaps to 6 in the routing policy last week. More parallel prefetch = more parallel JS evaluation during hydrate.
Devon: Both are plausible. Intl polyfill increases parse size; higher prefetch concurrency increases simultaneous JS work. Can we quickly test which one is dominant?
Maya: Action plan proposal: 1) rollback telemetry-client on canary -> telemetry-client@1.4.0 2) reduce prefetch concurrency to 2 3) rerun canary at 10% 4) gather sourcemaps + flamegraphs
Aj: I'll prepare a minimal telemetry patch that strips the intl polyfill and lazy-inits opentelemetry after hydrate. Will hold off full rollout until flagged.
Kevin: I'll open an urgent routing policy change to set `prefetch.maxConcurrent=2` behind a quota flag so we can toggle quickly.
deploy-bot: Deploy canary-frontend-v6 -> status: success (2:58 PM)
sre-bot: Alert: canary failure rate 4.6% over 5m, increased p95 render latency. Notifying @eng-platform
Maya: Started rollback to telemetry-client@1.4.0 on canary (kubectl rollout undo for the canary revision). Will patch routing policy after rollback completes.
Ryan: After rollback p95 is coming down to ~140ms on canary. Looks like telemetry bump was the primary culprit, but let's keep prefetch lowered while we validate.
Devon: Please collect longtask traces and the parse flamegraph for locale-heavy pages. We want to confirm polyfill parse cost vs concurrency effects.
Aj: On it. Also adding a CI size-budget check: fail the PR if bundle delta > 300KB and require manual approval for telemetry-like deps.
Kevin: I'll follow up with the quota flag PR and a short-runbook for toggling prefetch per-model route.
Maya: If the rollback stabilizes, we'll schedule a staged rollout with telemetry feature flags, size budget gates, and a canary at 5/20/50. Keeping this thread for followups.
Ryan: Agreed. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Maya: tagging @eng-platform for visibility and linking the incident ticket once we file it.
